descriptionChirho: A wind instrument, a reed flute or pipe, used in both celebratory and mournful contexts in ancient Israel. Appears in singular and plural forms with various prepositions: listed among instruments of prophetic ecstasy (1 Samuel 10:5), as part of banquet revelry ignoring God's works (Isaiah 5:12), accompanying joyful procession to the mountain of the Lord (Isaiah 30:29), played at Solomon's coronation celebration (1 Kings 1:40), and as a simile for the mournful sound of Moab's lamentation (Jeremiah 48:36, twice). The multilingual glosses are entirely consistent: mizmar/nay (Arabic), flute (English/French), bansuri (Hindi), piri (Korean), flauta (Spanish). All occurrences refer to the same musical instrument.
